verdict.reasoning: Patient states: "I keep having a headache."
Patient says: "It started yesterday... Yesterday, about mid morning."
Doctor asks about past headaches; patient replies: "Not really," indicating no significant prior history of headaches.
Patient describes location: "It's on the left side at the back" and confirms "Just on the left side?" "Yes." This corresponds to left posterior/occipital region only.
Patient: "Just quite intense and kind of quite throbbing. It kind of built up gradually over a short period of time" and rates it "Say about 8" on a 0–10 scale.
Doctor asks about nausea; patient: "No, nothing."
Doctor asks "Any nausea, vomiting..." and later "Are you feeling sick or vomiting or anything?"; patient responds "No, nothing" / "No, nothing like that."
Doctor asks "Any blurred vision or any pain over your eyes?"; patient: "No." This supports denial of visual changes.
Doctor: "Any funny lights or anything like that in your vision area? Any problems when you look into the light?" Patient: "No." Denies photophobia/light sensitivity.
Doctor: "Any high fever? Are you feeling shivery, sweaty?" Patient: "No, no fever."
Doctor: "Any rashes at all?" Patient: "No."
Neck stiffness is never asked about or mentioned; the transcript does not document denial of neck stiffness.
Doctor: "Any... tingling, numbness, weakness anywhere?" Patient: "No, nothing." This covers denial of focal weakness.
Same question: "Any... tingling, numbness, weakness anywhere?" Patient: "No, nothing." Denies numbness or tingling.
Doctor asks if position/Valsalva change pain: "any difference if you lie down, stand up, bend over, cough or sneeze or anything like that?" Patient: "No."
Doctor: "And last night, did you manage to sleep through the night?" Patient: "Yes, I did."
Patient: "I took some Nurofen yesterday." Doctor: "did that make any difference?" Patient: "Not really." (minimal relief).
Doctor: "have you got any other medical problems?" Patient: "No, I haven't."
Past surgical history is not discussed anywhere in the transcript.
Patient: "I took some Nurofen yesterday... Ibuprofen."
Doctor asks: "Any over the counter medications or allergies?" Patient lists Nurofen only and does not explicitly deny allergies; no statement of "no allergies" is made.
Patient: "My mother's had hypertension..."
Same sentence: "My mother's had hypertension and she does get migraines."
Doctor: "Who do you live with at home?" Patient: "My partner."
Doctor: "what's your job day to day?" Patient: "I'm a designer."
Doctor: "do you smoke at all normally?" Patient: "No, I don't."
Doctor: "Do you drink any alcohol regularly?" Patient: "No."
Doctor: "And any other drugs?" Patient: "No."
The transcript contains no vital signs, no physical examination findings, and no diagnostic studies.

New-onset (started yesterday) severe left posterior throbbing headache rated 8/10 is described; patient denies neurologic deficits (no numbness, tingling, weakness), visual symptoms, fever, vomiting; neck stiffness is not asked/denied but the assessment description otherwise matches the documented features.
Family history: "My mother's had hypertension and she does get migraines." This is noted by the clinician in the conversation.

Doctor: "trying slightly stronger pain relief... taking it instead of ibuprofen, not at the same time, and taking that regularly with food" and refers to "medication that I prescribed from the pharmacy."
Doctor: "You can take paracetamol along with that."
Doctor: "Try and take rest..."
Doctor: "have lots of good hydration."
Doctor: "if the pain's getting worse or you get new symptoms, feel fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, or you keep getting episodes of the same type of thing, then we need to speak to you..."

Doctor: "If it's getting worse or not settling in the next day or two, then certainly give us a call back when you try the medication that I prescribed from the pharmacy." This corresponds to 24–48 hours.
